findings.summary: runs view races the hook's claim and raises on a message claimed mid-read
findings.text: `pending_messages` lists the inbox and the same list is then stat()ed and read; a hook claiming a message between the two makes path.stat() raise FileNotFoundError, so a named-run view that is meant to report what is queued instead fails with an unhandled exception exactly when a delivery is in progress. The docstring claims the view cannot disagree with the delivery; it can also crash on it.

findings.summary: a claimed message that fails to read is lost with no receipt
findings.text: After `claim()` has moved a message into inbox/claimed/, a read failure is swallowed with `continue`: the message is neither delivered nor receipted and will never be retried, so the claim's exactly-once guarantee degrades to silent loss for that message.

findings.summary: third copy of the hook-group recogniser already in install.py
findings.text: `is_worker_inbox_group` repeats, line for line, the recogniser bodies already present at reckon/hooks/install.py:445 (`is_worker_walk_guard_group`) and reckon/hooks/install.py:470 (`is_worker_git_guard_group`), differing only in the matcher and script name; a third copy means a fix to the interpreter-bound recognition has three places to land. A shared predicate parameterised by script name would serve all three.

findings.summary: config-home resolver duplicated from reckon/_store.py and drifts from it
findings.text: `_config_home` re-implements reckon/_store.py:130 `_config_home`, the module that documents itself as the shared resolver; the copy also drops its `.resolve()` on the RECKON_HOME override, so a symlinked or trailing-slash RECKON_HOME resolves differently here than everywhere else. A lazy import inside this function would match the lazy `reckon._store` import the same module already makes in write_message.

findings.summary: evidence record contradicts crew tell's actual refusal order
findings.text: The evidence fragment states the reachability test is the run home's settings file "not the record's fenced flag", but reckon/crew_run_commands.py:2547 refuses on `record.get("fenced") is not True` before the settings file is consulted, so a fenced-false run whose home does carry the hook is refused. The record's account of why a run is refused disagrees with the code; the manifest evidence_inputs repeats the same claim.

findings.summary: reconciled assertions compare against the function they are testing
findings.text: `_with_inbox_hook` builds the expected settings bytes from `install.worker_inbox_group()`, the same function the seeder under test calls, so the assertion at line 157/222 holds whatever that function emits — a regression in the group's command, interpreter or matcher leaves it true. The independent check lives at tests/test_worker_inbox.py:381 (`Path(commands[0].split()[-1]).name == "worker_inbox.py"`); the same self-referential shape is used at tests/test_harness_home_carries_the_operator_config.py:206.

findings.summary: intermediate commit wrote a census file outside the fence, later reverted
findings.text: Commit 6e33b1a487 added seven lines to this file to declare the new writer, though it is named by neither the node's declared write paths nor the five paths granted through crew widen; commit cb1dcad073 then removed them, so the net head is unchanged and the manifest discloses the edit. The dispatch's own suite template does name this file in the node's scope, which is the contradiction worth closing in the dispatch contract rather than blaming the worker for.
